candidates.exact_span: Discharges from similar drinking water facilities (e.g City of Las Vegas, Village of Ruidoso, City of Springer etc) are required to meet effluent limitations for total suspended solids (TSS) at monthly average of 20 mg/l and daily maximum of 30 mg/l. Therefore, based on these similar permitted facilities, using BPJ, effluent limitations for TSS are established in the draft permit identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether these TSS numeric limits are enforceable in the draft permit, and whether the monthly-average versus daily-maximum limit applies to a given monitoring period, would change which limit is compared to reported TSS measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Loading limits are not established since the discharge is not a continuous one and is discharged from a holding lagoon on an as needed basis. This is identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether loading limits are absent versus concentration limits only affects applicable numeric limits (A). Interpreting discharge as non-continuous and as-needed affects when monitoring obligations attach to discharge events (B) and how to classify periods with no reported results as no-discharge, conditionally not required, or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether water-quality-based effluent limits are triggered beyond the stated technology-based TSS limits would change which enforceable numeric limits are deemed applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The stream mile distance from the WTP to the Confluence of San Juan River then further to the Navajo Nation boundary (West of the Confluence of La Plata River) is over 18 miles (>18 miles). The low flow of the San Juan River after the Animas River comingles, but upstream of the Farmington wastewater treatment plant, is approximately 278.6 MGD, meaning the flow from the Aztec Water treatment plant is less than approximately 0.064% of the flow in the San Juan River as it enters the Navajo Nation waters. 40 CFR §122.4(d) requires NPDES permits also be protective of a downstream state or tribe’s water quality standards, due to the nature of the discharge being from a water treatment plant, the low (0.177 MGD) volume of discharges, dilution with first the Animas River and then the San Juan River, and distance prior to entering the Navajo Nation, the water quality standards of the Navajo Nation will not be affected
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of stated distances, receiving-water flows, discharge volume (0.177 MGD), dilution, and the conclusion that Navajo Nation water quality standards will not be affected could change whether additional water-quality-based numeric limits or downstream-protection conditions are treated as applicable beyond the stated TSS limits.

candidates.exact_span: Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether technology-based TSS limits are deemed sufficient to protect water quality and designated uses affects whether additional water-quality-based numeric limits must be included in the set of applicable enforceable limits.

candidates.exact_span: The discharge from the facility may enter Lower Animas Ditch / Hampton Arroyo and/or Williams Arroyo in Water body
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which receiving water body or bodies the discharge enters determines which state water quality standards and criteria are used to derive applicable effluent limits, so different readings of this routing language could change the applicable numeric limits.
